Abu Talha gave his beloved Bairuha garden to his relatives on the Prophet's advice; after urging women to give alms, the Prophet told Zainab her husband and children deserved hers.
Zainab earns a double reward for giving Zakat to her husband and the orphans in her care, and Um Salama is rewarded for spending on Abu Salama's children.
Hearing verse 3.92, Abu Talha gives his beloved garden Beeruha in charity and the Prophet suggests he divide it among relatives; an honest treasurer is one of two charitable persons.
Whoever spends a pair of things in Allah's cause will be called by Paradise's gatekeepers, and the Prophet hopes Abu Bakr will be among them.
Hudhaifa said the verse about spending and not throwing oneself into destruction was revealed concerning spending in Allah's Cause.
When the verse on spending what you love was revealed, Abu Talha gave his beloved Bairuha garden in Allah's Cause, and on the Prophet's advice divided it among his relatives.
The generous and the miser are like two men in iron cloaks: the generous one's spreads to cover him when he spends, while the miser's rings stick tight.
Abu Talha gave his beloved Bairuha garden, where the Prophet drank, in charity when the verse on spending what one loves came, dividing it among his kin as advised.
The Prophet said Muslims are the last but will be foremost on Resurrection; the narrators add that Allah tells man to spend, promising to compensate him.
